task.title: rmap bundles selector listing
acceptance_criteria: New subcommand `rmap bundles` lists every declared `[bundles.*]` entry — agent-discoverable replacement for `grep '^\[bundles\.' roadmap/tasks.toml`. Closes the ergonomics gap where `rmap next --bundle` requires already knowing the bundle name.

New module src/bundles.rs holds `BundleSummary { name, phase, phase_name, order, description, task_count, status_counts, next_task, in_focus }` plus pure `list_bundles(tasks, filter) -> Vec<BundleSummary>`. Per-bundle `next_task` is computed by reusing `next::next_task` with a `TaskFilter { bundle: Some(name), .. }` — do NOT duplicate the dep-satisfaction logic.
Sort order: focus-phase bundles first (matching `tasks.focus.phase`), then by `phase.order` asc, then by `bundle.order` asc. `in_focus = (phase == tasks.focus.phase)`.

Human stdout: one line per bundle grouped under a `phase <N> — <phase_name>  [<phase_status>{, focus}]` header. Row shape: `<bundle_name>    <done>/<total> <status_glyph_or_next>  — <description>`. Status_glyph_or_next rules, evaluated in order: (1) all-done → `✅`; (2) pending=0 and in_progress>0 → `🚧`; (3) pending=0 and in_progress=0 and blocked>0 → `all-blocked ⛔`; (4) pending>0 and `next::next_task` returns None (every pending task has an unsatisfied in-repo dependency) → `pending:<n> (deps unmet) ⏸` where <n> is the pending count; (5) otherwise → `next:<id> [Eff:<eff>] <tier_glyph>`.
Reuses `scoring::format_efficiency` and `scoring::tier_glyph` — never folds the glyph into format_efficiency (load-bearing invariant for Eff tier glyphs).

`--json` envelope: `{ "schema_version": 1, "focus_phase": <u32|null>, "bundles": [BundleSummary, ...] }`. Always emits the `bundles` array (possibly empty). `next_task` is either null or `{ id, title, eff }` with eff as a number (not a formatted string). `status_counts` always emits all four keys: pending, in_progress, done, blocked (zero-filled).
Flags: `--json`, `--phase <N>`, `--has-next` (only bundles with non-null next_task), `--in-focus` (only bundles where in_focus == true). Flags compose with AND semantics.
Empty-state: zero declared bundles → stdout `(no bundles declared)`, JSON emits empty `bundles: []`, exit 0. Zero bundles after filter → stdout `(no bundles match filter)`, empty JSON array, exit 0.

task.title: rmap next-bundle: select one session-sized bundle (Option 1: bundle = session, no subsetting)
acceptance_criteria: New `rmap next-bundle` subcommand. Flags: `--phase <N>` (override focus), `--bundle <name>` (force-pick), `--json`, `--tasks-path`. Emits a bundle picked per the ranking rule plus every currently-actionable pending task in that bundle in dep-topological order.

Ranking rule: focus-phase bundles win over non-focus; within a phase, rank by sum-of-Eff over the bundle's dep-satisfied pending tasks (descending); ties broken by `bundles.<name>.order` ascending; bundles with zero actionable pending tasks (all-done, all-blocked, or all deps unmet) are skipped.

No auto-subsetting (Option 1). Output is *all* dep-satisfied pending tasks in the chosen bundle — never a D-budget slice. Bundle sizing is the author's responsibility; oversized bundles get split in `tasks.toml`, not windowed here.

Human output: header line `bundle <name>  phase <N> — <phase_name>  [<bundle_done>/<bundle_total>]  — <description>` followed by one row per task using the same row shape as `rmap list` (id, status glyph, title, `[D/B/U → Eff:x.y] <tier_glyph>`). Empty pick prints a single line `none — no actionable bundle in <phase or 'any phase'>` to stderr (exit 0).

JSON envelope: `{ schema_version, focus_phase, bundle: { name, phase, description } | null, tasks: [ExportedTask, ...] }`. Empty pick → `bundle: null`, `tasks: []`. Tasks reuse `ExportedTask` (so `eff` is included). Renaming or removing any envelope key is a `schema_version` bump.

Dep-topological ordering inside the chosen bundle: tasks emitted such that for every emitted task its `depends_on` entries either point outside the bundle (already done by invariant — dep-satisfied) or appear earlier in the output. Cycles inside a bundle are already rejected by `validate`, so the topological sort never fails.

Selector logic factored as `next_bundle::pick(tasks, filter, today) -> Option<BundlePick>` in a new `src/next_bundle.rs`. Reuses `next::next_tasks` / `query::matches_bundle` / `scoring::efficiency` / `bundles::list_bundles`-derived per-bundle state — no duplicated dep-satisfaction logic. Pure function; no I/O.

Tests: at least (a) focus-phase wins over a higher-sum-Eff bundle in another phase, (b) ties broken by `bundle.order`, (c) bundle with all-blocked tasks is skipped, (d) bundle whose only pending task has unmet deps is skipped, (e) `--bundle <name>` force-picks even when its sum-Eff is lower, (f) JSON shape stable (snapshot or field-presence asserts), (g) topological order assertion when bundle has internal `depends_on` chain. Smoke test in `tests/skills_smoke.rs` picks up the new `SKILLS.md` example automatically.

CLAUDE.md gains a Load-bearing-invariants bullet for the JSON envelope, the ranking-rule contract, the empty-pick line spelling, and the no-subsetting rule. Architecture section gets a `next_bundle.rs` entry. Files touched: src/next_bundle.rs, src/main.rs, src/export.rs, tests/cli.rs, SKILLS.md, CLAUDE.md.

task.title: rmap import — emit a paste-ready ROADMAP.md→tasks.toml migration prompt
acceptance_criteria: `rmap import` prints a paste-ready prompt instructing an agent to convert one or more hand-edited ROADMAP.md files into roadmap/tasks.toml

task.body:
Add an `rmap import` command that emits a paste-ready migration prompt — it does NOT parse ROADMAP.md itself. The command is the `rmap delegate` pattern applied to migration: it hands an agent a structured prompt; the agent does the conversion.

Why not a parser: a heuristic markdown parser would capture only the structured fields (phases, titles, score brackets, status glyphs) and punt on the prose bodies/acceptance_criteria — the hard 80%. An LLM does the whole job, adapts to any hand-edited ROADMAP.md shape, and migration is a one-time-per-repo cost run inside an agent session anyway.

Why a command and not include text: the migration knowledge (schema fields, marker-pair contract, validate/render/diff loop) has to live somewhere. Compiled into the binary and surfaced on demand via `rmap import` costs nothing per-session, stays discoverable through `rmap --help`, and can interpolate live `rmap schema` output so it never drifts. Putting it in the `rmap.md` include would tax every session of every consumer repo for a one-time job.

Surfaced by: migrating the claude-marketplace-elixir repo to rmap (2026-05-14) — the manual migration procedure works but every consumer repo pays the toil. Reuse `delegate.rs` as the structural precedent.

task.title: rmap status <id> done — auto-fill done_at (and started_at on in_progress)

task.body:
`rmap status <id> done` flips the task's `status` field but does not set `done_at`.
Same for `rmap status <id> in_progress` — it doesn't set `started_at`. Every `rmap
status` transition leaves the file internally inconsistent (status changed, lifecycle
timestamps missing), and downstream tooling that relies on `done_at` for recency
rendering (`render.rs` "recently done" tag) sees no timestamp.

Observed in `onchain_tempo` PR #1 (task 6 → done): CodeRabbit flagged both
`roadmap/tasks.toml` and `roadmap/data.json` for missing `done_at` after the status
flip — universal gap across consumers, not project-specific.

`src/mutate.rs::update_status_many_str` writes only `task["status"] = new_status`
(line 135). The canonical-order key index already reserves slots for `started_at`
(18) and `done_at` (20), so writing them is just an additional `task["done_at"] =
today()` when transitioning into `done`, mirrored for `started_at` on
`pending → in_progress`.

When transitioning OUT of `done` (e.g. re-opening a task), keep the existing
`done_at` intact unless the caller explicitly clears it — preserves audit trail.

Out of scope: backfilling done_at on already-done tasks with no timestamp (separate
doctor-fix task); phase-level status rollups (separate concern).
task.implemented: update_status_many_str now auto-fills done_at / started_at on the respective transitions when absent; existing values never overwritten; canonical_task_key_index sort triggers only on new-insert.

task.title: `rmap new --from-stdin` rejects `out_of_scope` though `rmap schema` declares it
acceptance_criteria: `rmap new --from-stdin` accepts `out_of_scope = ["..."]` on a `[[task]]` block without erroring
`rmap show <id>` renders an `out_of_scope:` section listing the bullets, mirroring `acceptance_criteria` rendering
`rmap show <id> --json` emits `out_of_scope` as an array (empty `[]` when unset, mirroring `acceptance_criteria`)
`rmap delegate <id>` renders an `## Out of scope` section in the prompt body when populated, omits it when empty
Round-trip test: a task authored with `out_of_scope` survives `rmap render` + re-read without losing the field
task.body:
`rmap schema` lists `out_of_scope` under `[[task]]` properties (`{ default: [], type: array, items: { type: string } }`), identical shape to `acceptance_criteria`. But the `--from-stdin` deserializer's `[[task]]` struct doesn't include the field — attempting to author a task with `out_of_scope` fails with:

    unknown field `out_of_scope`, expected one of `id`, `phase`, `bundle`, `title`, `scores`,
    `markers`, `depends_on`, `linear_id`, `assignee`, `module`, `model`,
    `acceptance_criteria`, `body`, `created_at`, `scored_at`

The schema and the parser have drifted — schema says supported, parser says no. Either:

(a) wire the field through (deserializer, `rmap show`, `rmap show --json`, `rmap delegate` template); preferred since `~/.claude/includes/task-writing.md` calls out `## Out of scope` as a recommended issue-body section that authors currently have to inline-prose into `body`. Promoting it to structured metadata makes `rmap delegate`'s prompt rendering consistent across the documented section list, and lets agents query the field directly.

(b) drop it from the JSON schema. The schema currently misleads — agents reading `rmap schema` reasonably conclude the field is supported.

(a) is the right call given the task-writing template already canonicalizes the section. The fix is mechanical: add the field to the `Task` deserialize struct, plumb through the rendering paths, mirror the `acceptance_criteria` test cases.

**Reproduction:**

    cd <any rmap-managed repo>
    rmap new --from-stdin <<'EOT'
    [[task]]
    phase = 1
    title = "smoke"
    scores = { d = 1, b = 1, u = 1 }
    out_of_scope = ["x"]
    body = "y"
    EOT
    # Error: parse stdin TOML: ... unknown field `out_of_scope`

Surfaced from a ccxt_ocx session that wanted to capture out-of-scope notes on a task refinement; folded into `body` prose as workaround.

task.body:
When a task undergoes significant design evolution during implementation (heavy plan-mode iteration, ratings feedback, discovery of better shapes, etc.), the original `body` in tasks.toml becomes historical intent rather than an accurate record of what shipped.

Example: ccxt_ocx Task 4 (`CcxtOcx.Error`). The task was originally written with one set of tags, return shapes, and API surface. After cross-plan ratings and synthesis, the delivered module used a meaningfully different (better) design. The original body no longer described reality, but we had no clean place to record the final outcome while preserving the original spec.

Add an `implemented` field (parallel to `body`) with conditional-required validation:

- `body` = original task definition / intent (never mutated after creation)
- `implemented` = what was actually built and why — REQUIRED when `status = "done"`, optional/absent on pending/in_progress/blocked
- The Rust type is `Option<String>` because pending tasks have nothing to record, but `validate.rs` enforces `Some` on done (same conditional-required pattern as `blocked_reason` when `status = "blocked"`)

For trivial tasks where the delivery matched the body exactly, a short `implemented = "as specified in body"` (or a one-line `shipped in <commit>` echo) is fine — the field's value is in being durable, not in being long. The cost of writing one line is low; the auditability payoff (future agents reading old roadmaps, post-mortem analysis, project archaeology) is durable.

This field should be:
- Validated as conditionally required on done (the new contract)
- Rendered by `rmap show` and `rmap delegate` (as a distinct section after the original body)
- Included in `data.json` and JSON output
- Omitted from ROADMAP.md task tables (like `model`, `assignee`, etc.)

Proposed name: `implemented`. Alternatives to consider during implementation: `delivery`, `outcome`, `actual`.

Backfill question (decide during impl): rmap's own tasks.toml already has ~6 done tasks lacking this field, plus any other rmap-using project. Two viable strategies — one-time stub backfill (`implemented = "<see body and shipped_in commit>"`), or temporary softening that only enforces on `done_at >= <cutoff>`. The schema_version bump is the migration boundary either way.
task.implemented: Added Task::implemented: Option<String> field, conditionally required when status=done (mirrors blocked_reason pattern). Three-place edit + schema_version bump 1→2. Consumer-first extensions over and above the AC: --implemented flag on rmap status (single-step UX), interactive TTY prompt, visual body/implemented distinction in rmap show, project-CLAUDE.md consuming-agent-POV rule. acceptance_criteria: `rmap depend 2 on 1` succeeds on a fixture containing string-id tasks `"1"` and `"2"`

task.body:
`rmap depend` rejects in-repo dependency edges whose target task id is a numeric-only string (e.g. `"7"`, `"1"`), even though the target exists and `rmap show <id>` resolves the same id correctly.

Reproduction (minimal — `schema_version = 1` project with three tasks `"1"`, `"2"`, `"2b"`):

```
$ rmap depend 2 on 1
Error: …/tasks.toml:30: task 2 depends on unknown task 1

$ rmap depend 2b on 1
Error: …/tasks.toml:38: task 2b depends on unknown task 1

$ rmap depend 2 on 2b
(succeeds — depends_on edge written)
```

The source-id format doesn't matter; only the target's format does. Anything with a non-digit character in the target id resolves; pure-digit string ids do not. `rmap show 1 --json`, `rmap show 7 --json` resolve correctly — so the storage layer keys correctly on the string id. The bug is local to the `depend` command's target-id lookup, likely parsing the target argument as an integer (or coercing to one) before looking it up against a string-keyed map.

Workaround: edit `depends_on = [...]` directly in `roadmap/tasks.toml`; `rmap validate` accepts the resulting state.

Originally hit while running `rmap depend 18 on 7` in the ccxt_ocx project (Task 18 → Task 7). Real-world scenarios with numeric-only ids include any project that started auto-numbering tasks (1, 2, 3, …) before introducing variant suffixes.
task.implemented: add_dependency_str now mirrors the target task's id storage shape via target_id_shape (Integer | Text), so `rmap depend <src> on <numeric-only-string-id>` reconciles correctly at validation time.

acceptance_criteria: `[milestones.<name>]` top-level table accepted in tasks.toml (parallel to `[phases.N]` / `[bundles.NAME]`) with fields: name, description, order, status (pending|active|done), target_version (optional)

Linear `Milestone` backfill via MCP — separate task; the schema lands first, sync second
Marker-vocab expansion — milestones replace the would-be `to-prod` marker; no marker work in this task
task.body:
rmap has phases (sequential work bundles), bundles (topical grouping), and markers (execution / delegation / quality modifiers) — but no first-class concept for *which release ships a task*. Real release lines cross phases: a `v1.0` cut typically pulls work from multiple phases while deferring others to `v-next`. Today this is unrepresentable in tasks.toml without smuggling it into markers (rejected — see § "Why not a marker") or naming-convention bundles (rejected — bundles are phase-bound by design).

Add `milestones` as a first-class top-level concept parallel to phases and bundles:

```toml
[milestones.v0_1]
name = "v0.1 — first usable"
description = "Macro-generated data plane on one exchange end-to-end"
target_version = "0.1.0"
order = 1
status = "active"

[milestones.v1_0]
name = "v1.0 — production-ready trade plane"
description = "Full unified CCXT surface incl. signed trade plane, testnet-verified"
target_version = "1.0.0"
order = 2
status = "pending"

[[task]]
id = 7
phase = 2
bundle = "macros"
milestone = "v0_1"
# ...
```

## Why not a marker

Markers describe *how* to work on a task (parallel-safe, delegate to Codex, this is a bug, this is a security item). Milestones describe *which release ships it* — a relationship to a release line, not a modifier. Marker-vocab bloat is the failure mode if we conflate the two — `to-prod`, `to-v1.0`, `to-v0.1`, `to-v2.0` would all be markers under that model, and any task without one of them becomes ambiguous (post-release? backlog? unknown?). A first-class relationship is the right shape.

## Why not a bundle

Bundles are phase-bound — `bundles.<name>.phase` is required. Release lines are explicitly cross-phase: v1.0 pulls from phases 2, 3, 4, 5 simultaneously. Twisting bundles to do this would either require dropping the phase constraint (breaking change to existing bundle semantics) or introducing fake phases for release-line grouping. Neither is clean.

## Composition with existing concepts

| Concept   | Role today                | After milestones                                |
|-----------|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| phase     | sequential work ordering  | unchanged — "what order to build"               |
| bundle    | topical grouping          | unchanged — "what belongs together"             |
| markers   | execution modifiers       | unchanged — "how to work on it"                 |
| milestone | (missing)                 | **"which release ships it"** — flat, cross-phase|

A task can carry phase + bundle + milestone independently. Queries compose: `rmap next --milestone v1_0 --bundle macros` shows the next macros-bundle task that's in the v1.0 release cut.

## Open design questions (decide during impl)

- **Status auto-derivation** — does a milestone flip to `done` automatically when all member tasks are `done`, or only via explicit `rmap milestone-status`? Lean: manual for v1, auto-derivation as a follow-up if friction surfaces.
- **ROADMAP.md render placement** — three viable shapes: (a) milestone tag in each row's prefix (like `[v1.0]`), (b) a top-level "Release Lines" section that lists each milestone with member tasks, (c) both. Lean: (a) for inline visibility + (c) only if (a) feels noisy.
- **Linear sync** — Linear has `Milestone` as a native concept reachable via `mcp__linear-server__list_milestones`. Out of scope for this task; once schema lands, a follow-up can sync.

## Migration

Schema_version bumps. Existing tasks default to `milestone = None`. No retroactive backfill — the schema lands empty and projects populate as they define their release lines. ccxt_ocx is the immediate consumer (will define `v0_1` data-plane and `v1_0` trade-plane milestones on first migration).

## Origin

Surfaced from a ccxt_ocx scoping conversation. Attempt was to add a `to-prod` marker for the "release-readiness cut," rejected as marker-vocab bloat. The deeper observation: production-readiness is the implicit goal of every roadmap task; what's actually missing is a way to pin tasks to specific release lines. Hence milestones — relationship, not tag.

task.title: Task outcome layer — delivered_by + verified fields
acceptance_criteria: `rmap status <id> done --delivered-by <agent> --verified` persists both fields and still accepts --implemented alongside them
`delivered_by` and `verified` surface in `rmap show`, `roadmap/data.json` (ExportedTask), and `rmap diff`

Neither field appears on StdinTask / NewTaskFields — they are transition-time only

Validating delivered_by against an agent registry — free-text like `model`; a [agents.*] table is a separate future task
Backfilling existing done tasks — the fields land empty and populate going forward
Enriching `verified` beyond a bool (check-stack name, separate timestamp) — done_at is close enough; revisit only if the bool proves insufficient
task.body:
The Task schema records intent (`scores`, `model`, `assignee`, `files_to_modify`) and the implementer's self-report (`implemented` — free-text prose). It has no structured slot for two facts every cross-session consumer needs cold: which agent actually delivered the task, and whether an evaluator separate from the implementer confirmed it. Today both are buried in `implemented` prose ("Delivered by Grok in the dogfood batch; verified green by the check stack") — readable, but not queryable — and `done` alone cannot distinguish a verification-graded task from one an implementer simply declared finished.

Add two optional transition-time fields:

- `delivered_by` (Option<String>) — the agent or instance that executed the task. Distinct from `model` (the *intended* model) and `assignee` (the *owner*); this records who actually did the work. Free-text and unvalidated, like `model` — agent identifiers churn.
- `verified` (Option<bool>) — whether an evaluator separate from the implementer confirmed the task: `true` = an independent check passed (a verification stack went green, a code-review session approved); absent = not independently graded (hand-built, bootstrap, merged directly). This encodes the evaluator-separation principle — `done` means "an implementer said so", `verified` means "a grader agreed".

Both are transition-time fields set alongside `implemented` at `rmap status <id> done` — add `--delivered-by <agent>` and `--verified` flags to that mutator. They deliberately take the lighter mirror path the Task doc-comment describes for transition-time fields (`set_status_str` + `canonical_task_key_index` + `diff_fields!` + `ExportedTask` + `schema.rs`), NOT the six-surface creation path — they never belong on `StdinTask` / `NewTaskFields`.

`rmap show` renders both prominently on a done task, so a fresh instance sees the outcome without reading prose. `rmap list` gains a `--delivered-by <agent>` filter — the roadmap becomes an agent-delivery ledger as a free side effect of normal completion. `rmap doctor` gains a soft advisory: a `done` task with `verified` absent is surfaced as "claimed, not graded", never as an error (hand-built tasks are legitimate). Purely additive optional fields — no `schema_version` bump, mirroring the Task 19 `model` and Task 24 milestone precedent.

task.title: rmap new allocates a colliding task id on a string-id roadmap
acceptance_criteria: `rmap new` on a string-id roadmap (`id = "1"`) allocates max+1, not 1
An auto-allocated id is serialized in the roadmap's existing form — string for a string-id file, integer for an integer-id file
Integer-id roadmaps (rmap's own) are byte-identical — no regression
Unit tests cover string-id allocation, string-id serialization, and integer-id no-regression
task.body:
`next_task_id` (src/mutate.rs) computed the next auto-allocated id by scanning existing tasks with `value.as_integer()` — which matches only TOML integer-typed ids. `TaskId` is dual-form: a roadmap may store ids as integers (`id = 28`, rmap's own convention) or as numeric strings (`id = "28"`, the convention harness's roadmap uses). On a string-id roadmap every `as_integer()` returned `None`, so `max` stayed 0 and `next_task_id` returned 1 — silently allocating a task whose id collided with the existing `id = "1"`. The colliding task was unreachable by `rmap show`, and `rmap validate` did not catch it because duplicate detection keys on `TaskId`, whose `Number(1)` and `Text("1")` are distinct values.

A second defect compounded it: the allocated id was always serialized as a TOML integer, so even a corrected allocation would write `id = 29` into a file of `id = "28"` strings, drifting the id type.

Fix `next_task_id` to count both integer and numeric-string ids, and serialize an auto-allocated id in the form the roadmap already uses so `rmap new` never mixes the two within one file. Surfaced while filing audit follow-up tasks into the harness roadmap (a string-id roadmap) — the same class of bug as the earlier f09ac55 incident.
task.implemented: Fixed next_task_id to count numeric-string ids (new task_id_value_as_u32 helper) so a string-id roadmap continues its sequence instead of restarting at 1; add_task_str serializes the allocated id in the file's existing form (new ids_are_string_typed helper) so integer and string id forms are never mixed within one file. 3 unit tests in mutate.rs cover string-id allocation, string-id serialization, and integer-id no-regression. Full cargo test suite + clippy green.

task.title: rmap validate does not detect duplicate task ids
acceptance_criteria: `rmap validate` fails a roadmap with two tasks sharing an id
A collision between an integer id and the string form of the same number (`id = 1` vs `id = "1"`) is detected
A decision is recorded on whether `TaskId`'s `Eq`/`Hash` should normalize numeric-string ids, fixing dependency / cycle validation on mixed-form files
Tests cover same-form and cross-form duplicate detection
out_of_scope: Auto-repairing a duplicated id — validation only reports
task.body:
`validate_tasks_str` (src/validate.rs) runs sixteen semantic checks but none asserts that task ids are unique. A roadmap with two tasks sharing an id — from a hand-edit, a botched `rmap import`, or a mutator bug — passes `rmap validate` clean. The integrity gate should reject a duplicated primary key.

The check is complicated by `TaskId` being dual-form (`Number(u32)` | `Text(String)`) with derived `Eq`/`Hash`: `Number(1)` and `Text("1")` hash and compare as distinct, so a naive `HashSet<TaskId>` would miss an `id = 1` / `id = "1"` collision. The same duality already makes `validate_dependencies` and `validate_dependency_cycles` latently wrong on a mixed-form file — a `depends_on` entry whose form differs from the target id's reads as an unknown task.

Add a `validate_unique_ids` check that normalizes each id to a canonical key (numeric-string ids fold to their number) before detecting collisions, and decide whether to give `TaskId` a normalizing `Eq`/`Hash` so dependency and cycle validation become correct on mixed files too. Discovered while fixing the `next_task_id` colliding-id bug — that bug's bad output reached disk precisely because validation could not see the collision.
task.implemented: Added validate_unique_ids (10th of 17 checks) and made TaskId Eq/Hash normalizing across Number(n)↔Text("n") canonical-key, so the same id in different disk forms (id = 1 vs id = "1") collides. Four call sites become correct on mixed-form files for free: validate_dependencies, validate_dependency_cycles, doctor.rs degenerate-bundle check, next_bundle.rs actionability memo — no edits to those sites; six new tests assert the regression on mixed forms. Cross-form error message uses TOML-literal forms (`duplicate task id "1" (already defined as 1)`) so the human can locate both lines; Display still strips quotes for the human-identity case. PartialEq<u32> also tightened to accept Text("1") == 1u32 for consistency with the normalizing Eq. Agent-grep contract substring: `duplicate task id`. Text ids that do not parse as u32 (e.g. "INE-5", "alpha") keep their own canonical key — Number(5) ≠ Text("INE-5"). No schema_version bump (purely additive validator + tighter in-memory equality; on-disk format and roundtrip unchanged). Docs: CLAUDE.md schema-invariants bullet + DESIGN.md schema-invariants paragraph.

task.body:
First consumer: the harness autonomous merge-train lander (harness Task 100) writes the merged commit SHA back to rmap on a successful land via `rmap status <id> done --verified --delivered-by <agent> --shipped-in <sha>`. Today `rmap status` exposes `--implemented`, `--delivered-by`, and `--verified`, but `shipped_in` has no status-time mutator — the field exists in the schema (schema.rs), exports (export.rs / ExportedTask), diff (diff.rs) and show (query.rs), yet can only be set by hand-editing tasks.toml. That hand-edit is exactly the "work around a gap in rmap" the harness contract forbids, so the lander needs a first-class flag.

Add a `--shipped-in <sha>` flag to the `Status` command and thread it through the existing transition-time outcome path the lighter mirror way — the same path `--delivered-by` already takes (status arg struct in main.rs -> `update_status` -> `update_status_many_str` / `update_status_str` in mutate.rs -> insert the `shipped_in` key + canonical key-order sort). It is `done`-only with a warn-and-ignore stderr note on other transitions, overwrites any existing value, and must never leak onto the creation surfaces. This completes the schema_outcome bundle: delivered_by (who), verified (graded?), shipped_in (where it landed) — the full queryable outcome triple.

Implementation details (flag name, exact insertion point, sort index — shipped_in is already index 27 in canonical_task_key_index) are for the implementing agent to derive from how --delivered-by is wired in sibling Task 28.

task.body:
First consumer: the harness autonomous merge-train lander (harness Task 101) needs a terminal sink for tasks it abandons after exhausting its landing-attempt cap. `rmap status <id> blocked` already flips status and `rmap next` skips blocked tasks, but there is no CLI path to record *why* — a blocked task with no machine-readable reason is an opaque dead end to an orchestrator scanning the roadmap. The lander writes a structured-ish string via `rmap status <id> blocked --reason "land-cap exhausted: post-merge-red x2 (task 101, integrated HEAD abc1234)"`.

The `blocked_reason` field already exists across schema/validation/export/diff (it was always required when status=blocked, but only settable by hand-editing tasks.toml — exactly the gap the harness contract forbids). Wire a `--reason` flag on `rmap status` mirroring the outcome-flag path (`--delivered-by` is the template), but gated on the `blocked` transition instead of `done`; render the reason inline on the blocked row; and auto-clear it when the task leaves blocked. Implementation details (exact gating, render placement, canonical key order) are for the implementing agent to derive from how the sibling outcome flags are wired.
